title: Quant triage lab notebook
content:
Topline: exploratory personal lab notebook for the NaN/quality regressions seen when enabling mixed precision + quantized kernels. This is messy — notes to self, commands I ran, short hypotheses, quick stack traces, and the small checks that either ruled things out or pointed fingers. Keep low-friction chronology so I can hand to Marco/lin later.

Background/context
- Model: rw-inference-microbert-v2 (decoder-only, 12 layers, fused attention).
- Baseline (no quant): torch 2.1, cuda 12.1, running FP32 and BF16 paths on A100s -> stable, eval ppl ~ 7.8 on small eval set.
- Experiments turning on INT8/FP8 kernels for inference path. Observed NaNs in logits / attention softmax divergence in a small percentage (~1-3%) of sequences; sometimes immediate, sometimes after a few tokens.
- Hypothesis space: activation overflow on softmax, KV cache accumulation causing scale blow-up, layernorm numerical edge-cases after quantization, per-channel scale mismatch during weight packing, or buggy kernel for special-case lengths.

Quick repro (minimal)
- Branch: quant/trial/fp8-int8-mix (local)
- Condensed command I used to repro locally: 
  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -u repro_quant_nan.py --model checkpoints/microbert-v2 --quant-config configs/quant_fp8_int8.json --dataset tiny_eval.json --seed 42 
- Observed output: at token step 4 many runs show: 
  WARNING: numeric-instability: softmax overflow detected (max>1e9)
  RuntimeError: NaN in logits at forward() +0.4s
- repro_quant_nan.py is a tiny harness that feeds same prompt repeatedly; sometimes NaN appears at step 2, sometimes step 10. Non-deterministic but much higher rate when using torch.compile(full=True) and flash-attn-2 kernel enabled.

Commands / env snapshots I tried (to rule out environment)
- python -c "import torch; print(torch.__version__, torch.cuda.is_available(), torch.version.cuda)" -> torch 2.1.0, cuda 12.1
- nvidia-smi confirms A100-SXM4, driver 535.xx
- pip list: bitsandbytes 0.40.0, triton 2.x, flash-attn==v2.0.3 (local build)
- run with different NCCL envs (NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1) no effect on single GPU run.

Small debugging checklist (what I ran and results)
- Re-run in FP32 only: no NaNs. Good -> points at quant path.
- BF16 only (no quant): stable.
- INT8-only (symmetric per-channel quantization on weights) on CPU via fake-quant: stable in unit test harness.
- INT8 runtime (GPU) via custom kernel: intermittent NaN.
- FP8-only (E4M3 and E5M2 configs tried): NaN appears more frequently than INT8.
- Turn off flash-attn: NaN frequency drops by ~70% (interesting).
- Disable layernorm fusion (use python layernorm): NaNs still appear but less frequent.
- Zero-out highest-magnitude weights in layer 7 (temporary) -> NaN frequency drops. Suggests weight outliers exacerbate.

Key error snippets I captured
- kernel trace: 
  RuntimeError: cuda kernel failed : device-side assert triggered at attention_kernels.cu:429
  stack: /workspace/model/attn.py:318 -> forward_attention() -> attention_kernels.cu:429
- python stack when softmax overflow: 
  ValueError: numeric instability: softmax input contains >1e6 in magnitude at decoder/layer_9/attn -> approx_exp underflow/overflow
- downstream: logits becomes NaN -> argmax fails -> sampling returns NaN -> client panics.

Small experiments (inputs/outputs)
- Dump activations of pre-softmax vector for runs with NaN vs without: max abs value in problem runs ~ 1e10, normal runs ~ 20-200. So some step blows up by many orders.
- Tracked KV cache magnitudes: observed monotonic growth in cached K values for certain sequences when using FP8. Hypothesis: quantized accumulation of KV (with rounding) that loses negative cancellation -> growth.
- Per-layer norms: layer7 and layer9 have largest delta in runs that go NaN.

Things I tried to mitigate (and outcome)
- Clip logits pre-softmax to [-1e3, 1e3]: prevents NaN but changes output distribution and PPL degrades a lot. Not acceptable as a long-term fix but good as a band-aid.
- Add tiny epsilon to softmax exp: stable but slightly changes probabilities.
- Per-channel static rescaling of weights in suspect layers (scale down by 1/8): reduced NaN rate but introduced obvious quality regression in a few prompts.
- Use per-tensor FP8 scaling vs per-channel: per-channel reduced NaN rate — suggests per-channel scaling is safer here.
- Run with stochastic rounding off/on (bfloat emulation toggle): stochastic rounding reduced NaN incidence a little.

Reproduction notes for team handoff
- Repro script: repro_quant_nan.py (attached). Steps: checkout quant/trial/fp8-int8-mix, python repro_quant_nan.py --prompt-file test_prompts.txt --repeat 800 --seed 42. Expect NaN within first 200 tokens on A100 local.
- Minimal artifacts to share: small eval dataset (20 prompts) + model checkpoint with 8-bit packed weights in artifacts/pack-v1.

Hypotheses prioritized (ranked)
1) Quantized accumulation error in KV cache for FP8 combined with flash-attn fused kernels -> occasional runaway magnitudes (most likely). Evidence: turning off flash-attn reduces incidence; KV magnitudes show monotonic growth.
2) Weight outliers in specific layers get amplified by low dynamic range of E4M3 FP8 and a buggy per-channel scale computation in the packing script. Evidence: manually clamping top weights reduces frequency.
3) Softmax implementation inside fused kernel not guarding against extreme inputs (e.g., no subtract-max step in some code path). Evidence: observed extremely large pre-softmax logits; clipping mitigates.
4) Non-determinism of torch.compile combined with triton kernels producing rare memory corruption -> NaN. Evidence: slightly higher incidence with torch.compile(full=True). Lower priority but not dismissed.

Next steps (practical)
- Immediate: create small automated fuzz test that runs 1000 short prompts through FP8 kernels with and without flash-attn; collect layer max/mean stats per step and dump early when ratio > 1e4. (I sketched fuzz_runner.py)
- Re-run with kernel debug enabled (flash-attn debug build) to get more precise line of failure.
- Add defensive subtract-max in fused softmax path as a patch to test if that prevents explosion (quick A/B).
- Get Marco to produce a binary trace with ASAN for the custom kernel where device-side assert was triggered.
- Add unit that verifies per-channel scale values computed by packing script exactly match reference CPU computation (float64) within 1e-6. I have a test file pack_scale_check.py (TODO).

Notes to self / random scribbles
- When facing NaNs in quant, don't assume kernel driver first — quant accumulative effects can blow up slowly.
- Keep dataset of prompts that trigger failure (I put 12 in failure_prompts.txt). Some look adversarially designed (long runs of repeated tokens) which may amplify rounding.
- Consider introducing a small EMA normalization on KV cache as an engineering mitigation: slow roll normalization to keep magnitudes bounded. Will likely change generation behavior though.
- Checkpoint versions: pack-v1 vs pack-v2 differ in scale rounding method (v2 uses floor->int). Might be culprit.

Attached quick checklist to run before handing off:
- reproduce with flash-attn off (yes/no)
- reproduce with layernorm unfused (yes/no)
- dump per-layer max/mean for run that goes NaN
- run pack_scale_check.py between pack-v1 and pack-v2
- create GHPR with debug logs and add JIRA label MLINF-318

If handing to other engs: start with hypothesis #1 and try simple mitigation: disable flash-attn fused kernel and add subtract-max in softmax fused path; if that stabilizes, proceed to deeper analysis of KV accumulation numeric path.

Timestamped breadcrumb log (local)
- 2025-11-05 09:24 seed 42 initial discovery: intermittent NaN with FP8+flash-attn
- 2025-11-06 11:02 turned off flash-attn -> NaN rate down
- 2025-11-07 16:30 manually clamped layer7 weights -> NaN rate down further
- 2025-11-08 10:20 repro script added to branch quant/trial/fp8-int8-mix
- 2025-11-09 15:45 pack-v2 suspicion (packing rounding change), filed GHPR#5178
- 2025-11-11 09:10 compiled debug flash-attn build to run with ASAN

Final quick TODOs (me):
- flesh out fuzz_runner.py and land small GHPR that adds the automated fuzz job in CI (nightly) to catch regressions early.
- pair with Marco for kernel-level trace if ASAN points to memory corruption.
- document mitigation tradeoffs (clip vs per-channel rescale vs EMA KV norm) for product.

-- E.S.
